name: Bisi Bele Bath
cuisine: South Indian (Karnataka; an Udupi-restaurant staple in Matunga, Mumbai)

ingredients.name: Toor dal (split pigeon peas / arhar dal)
Carrot (gajar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ¼ medium carrot, in 1 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Potato (aloo)
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ¼ small potato, in 1 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Tamarind (imli)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a marble-sized piece (or ½ tsp thick paste)

ingredients.name: Bisi bele bath powder (homemade, below, or MTR / store-bought)

equipment: Medium saucepan or kadai, for boiling the vegetables in tamarind water and combining
Small pan or tadka pan, for the tempering
Heavy pan and a dry mixer/grinder jar, only if making the powder
Small bowl for soaking tamarind, strainer, ladle or masher, knife, chopping board, measuring spoons (normal teaspoons are fine)

steps.title: Roast the dals
steps.text: Heat ¼ tsp oil in a heavy pan on low. Add 2 tsp chana dal and 1 tsp urad dal.
steps.visualCue: The dals turn light golden and smell nutty.
steps.cameraCheck: The golden dals in the pan
steps.videoShot: Dals stirred in a pan, changing colour.

steps.title: Roast the seeds and whole spices
steps.text: Add 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin, ¼ tsp fenugreek, ½ tsp pepper, 2 cm cinnamon, 3 cloves and the marathi moggu. Keep stirring on low.
steps.tip: Fenugreek turns bitter if it browns too much; keep the heat low.
steps.visualCue: The coriander seeds darken one shade and the pan smells strongly aromatic.
steps.cameraCheck: The spice mix in the pan
steps.videoShot: Coriander and cumin seeds tossing in the pan.

steps.title: Roast the chillies and poppy seeds
steps.text: Add 8–10 byadgi chillies and 1 tsp poppy seeds; stir for 1 min.
steps.visualCue: The chillies puff slightly and turn crisp; do not let them blacken.
steps.videoShot: Red chillies crackling among the seeds.

steps.title: Roast the coconut
steps.text: Add 3 tbsp grated dry coconut and stir until just golden, then switch off.
steps.visualCue: The coconut is light golden at the edges.
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the coconut mixed in
steps.videoShot: Coconut flakes stirred into the spices.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Spread the mix on a plate.
steps.tip: Grinding while warm makes the powder clump and go stale faster.
steps.visualCue: Cool to the touch.
steps.cameraCheck: The cooled spices on the plate
steps.videoShot: Overhead shot of the colourful spice heap.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind to a fine powder in a dry mixer jar, in short pulses. Measure out 10 g (about 1½ tbsp) for today; store the rest in a dry, airtight jar.
steps.visualCue: An even, reddish-brown, fine powder.
steps.cameraCheck: 1½ tbsp powder in a small bowl
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting off the mixer jar to show the powder.

steps.title: Soak the tamarind
steps.text: Put a marble-sized piece of tamarind (5 g) in a small bowl with 60 ml warm water.
steps.visualCue: The tamarind sits submerged in the water.
steps.videoShot: Warm water poured over a tamarind ball.

steps.title: Wash the rice and dal
steps.text: Put 45 g rice and 30 g toor dal in a bowl; rinse 3 times and drain.
steps.visualCue: The last rinse water is only slightly cloudy.
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling rice and dal in water.

steps.title: Load the cooker
steps.text: Put the rice and dal in the cooker with 300 ml water and a pinch of turmeric. Stir.
steps.visualCue: Yellow-tinged water about 3 cm above the grains.
steps.videoShot: Turmeric dropped into the water.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Close and cook on medium for 4–5 whistles; switch off and let the pressure drop on its own.
steps.visualCue: 4–5 whistles counted.
steps.cameraCheck: The closed cooker on the stove
steps.videoShot: Steam puffing out with a whistle.

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Cut 25 g carrot and 25 g potato into 1 cm cubes, 20 g beans into 2 cm pieces, and peel and halve 4 small onions (25 g).
steps.tip: Keep the cubes small so they cook in the same time.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces; about 1 cup in total with the peas.
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped vegetables on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife cubing carrot.

steps.title: Extract the tamarind
steps.text: Squeeze the soaked tamarind with your fingers and strain the water; discard the seeds and fibres.
steps.visualCue: About 60 ml thin brown tamarind water.
steps.videoShot: Fingers squeezing tamarind pulp.

steps.title: Mix the masala paste
steps.text: Stir the 10 g bisi bele bath powder into 30 ml water to a smooth paste.
steps.tip: Adding dry powder straight to the pot makes lumps.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, lump-free, rust-red paste.
steps.cameraCheck: The paste in a small bowl
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring the red paste.

steps.title: Boil the vegetables
steps.text: In the saucepan, bring 90 ml water to a boil and add all the vegetables and 15 g peas.
steps.visualCue: A knife slides easily into a potato cube.
steps.videoShot: Vegetables tumbling into boiling water.

steps.title: Add tamarind, jaggery and masala
steps.text: Add the tamarind water, ½ tsp jaggery and the masala paste. Stir.
steps.visualCue: A reddish-brown, thin gravy around the vegetables.
steps.videoShot: The red paste swirling into the pan.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer on low-medium.
steps.visualCue: The raw tamarind smell is gone and the gravy thickens slightly.
steps.videoShot: Slow bubbles in the gravy.

steps.title: Mash the rice and dal
steps.text: Open the cooker and mash the rice and dal lightly with a ladle.
steps.visualCue: Soft and mushy, with some rice grains still visible.
steps.cameraCheck: A ladle of the mashed rice and dal
steps.videoShot: The ladle pressing the rice and dal.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Tip the rice-dal mixture into the gravy. Add the 2 g salt (less if the packet masala is salted) and stir well.
steps.visualCue: An even, orange-brown mix.
steps.videoShot: The rice-dal sliding into the red gravy.

steps.title: Adjust and simmer
steps.text: Add hot water a little at a time (up to 30 ml) and simmer on low, stirring so it does not stick.
steps.tip: It thickens a lot as it cools, so keep it looser than you want to eat it.
steps.visualCue: Loose and porridge-like; it drops slowly off the ladle and bubbles lazily.
steps.cameraCheck: A ladle lifted out of the pot
steps.videoShot: The thick mixture dripping from a ladle.

steps.title: Start the tempering
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp ghee in the small pan on medium-low; fry 4 cashews.
steps.visualCue: The cashews turn light golden.
steps.videoShot: Cashews sizzling in ghee.

steps.title: Add mustard and chilli
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp mustard seeds and the broken red chilli.
steps.visualCue: The mustard seeds pop and the chilli darkens slightly.
steps.cameraCheck: The popping mustard in the pan
steps.videoShot: Mustard seeds jumping in ghee.

steps.title: Add curry leaves and hing
steps.text: Add 6–8 curry leaves, then a pinch of hing; switch off.
steps.tip: Stand back; wet curry leaves splatter.
steps.visualCue: The curry leaves crackle and turn crisp.
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves spluttering.

steps.title: Pour the tempering
steps.text: Pour the tempering, with all the ghee, over the bisi bele bath and stir; sprinkle 1 tbsp chopped coriander.
steps.visualCue: Glossy, with golden cashews and dark curry leaves on top.
steps.videoShot: The sizzling tempering poured over the pot.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Cover for 2–3 min, then serve hot in a bowl, with khara boondi or chips on top at the table if you like (not counted).
steps.visualCue: Steaming, spoonable, reddish-brown bowl.
steps.videoShot: A spoon of boondi scattered on the hot bowl.

reasons: a boiled, not fried, one-pot meal that combines a grain and a pulse (about 15 g protein) with about 110 g vegetables, giving about 10 g fibre and good folate, magnesium, potassium and vitamin A. Against it: white rice makes it carb-heavy (about 75 g), 2 tsp ghee brings about a third of the day's saturated fat, and salt is about 2 g. Restaurant bowls tend to be richer in ghee, saltier, lighter on vegetables, and come topped with fried boondi or chips.

researchRating.basis: one of Karnataka's signature dishes, highlighted by Karnataka Tourism and on almost every darshini and Udupi menu in Bengaluru (Swiggy bestseller tags, a dedicated "best bisibele bath in Bengaluru" roundup), with many well-known recipe and masala-powder versions; in Mumbai it is praised at Matunga Udupi classics (Ram Ashraya in the Free Press Journal's oldest-Udupi list; a Cafe Madras review praising its tamarind-spice balance). Small deduction because it is labour-heavy at home, often relies on packet masala, and is hard to find on Mumbai delivery menus. Recipe review counts could not be verified in this run.

storage: Fridge: up to 2 days in an airtight box, refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking. Freezer: possible for up to 1 month (the potato turns slightly grainy). Reheat with 2–3 tbsp hot water, covered, in a pan on low for 4–5 min or the microwave for 2 min, stirring halfway; add the boondi only after reheating. The homemade powder keeps about 1 month in an airtight jar (longer in the fridge).
leftoverRemix: Bisi Bele Bath Tikki. Mix 1 cup cold, firm leftover bisi bele bath with 3 tbsp poha powder (or rice flour) and 1 tbsp chopped coriander; shape 4 small patties and shallow-fry on a tawa with 1 tsp oil per side until crisp (or air-fry at 190 °C for 12 min). Serve with curd or green chutney as a tangy evening snack.
burnOff: about 7.4 km of running (520 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 10.4 km of brisk walking (about 2 h at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). The boondi or chips topping adds about 1 km of running.

navratri.reason: rice, toor dal and onion are avoided on the common North and West Indian vrat rule set

ekadashi.reason: rice and dals (including toor dal) are the main foods given up on Ekadashi

jain.reason: skip potato, carrot and small onions (root vegetables and bulbs); rice, toor dal, tamarind, spices, ghee and above-ground vegetables fit common Jain practice

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal concern; a filling one-pot meal with about 15 g protein and 10 g fibre that suits sehri, though it is spicy and has about 2 g salt, so keep the chillies mild for the pre-dawn meal

jain.reason: skip potato, carrot and small onions (roots/bulbs); use capsicum, beans, peas and raw banana instead, and check a store-bought masala has no garlic or onion

vegan.reason: use 2 tsp groundnut oil instead of ghee

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, fish or egg, so it fits a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: the main recipe has no garlic; skip the 25 g small onions (many Karnataka Brahmin and temple versions already leave them out)

glutenFree.reason: rice and toor dal are gluten-free, but most hing (asafoetida) sold in India is compounded with wheat flour; use gluten-free (rice-flour) hing or skip it, and check a packet masala's label for hing

dairyFree.reason: ghee is the only dairy; replace it with groundnut oil

description: A vegetarian Karnataka one-pot of rice, toor dal and vegetables in a tamarind–spice gravy with ghee; Jain, vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free versions below.
